title: Minimum-Cost Bundle Cover
prompt:
Implement `minimum_cover(menu, wanted) -> tuple[int, list[tuple[int, int]]]`. Each menu entry is `(items, nonnegative_price)`. Return the minimum total price of a 0/1 selection that covers every distinct item in `wanted`, together with increasing-index `(bundle_index, 1)` pairs for the selected bundles. Contents absent from `wanted` have no effect.

Return `(-1, [])` when no selection covers all wanted items, and `(0, [])` when `wanted` is empty. If multiple selections have the same minimum cost, prefer the selection with fewer bundles; if still tied, choose the lexicographically smallest tuple of selected bundle indices.

The number of distinct wanted items is small enough for bitmask dynamic programming. A state represents the wanted items covered so far; skip a transition that adds no new wanted item. Aim for O(len(menu) * 2^k) state transitions for k distinct wanted items, plus deterministic tie handling.

example.reasoning: The second and third bundles cover all requested items for a total cost of five.
